title: QTc prolongation
draftNote: Content collected from the user, not yet written up. Kept outside server/data/adverse-effects/ so it is not published. Source tables: Maudsley 15th ed. Tables 1.35-1.38.

footnotes.lumateperone: Limited clinical experience; an association with QT prolongation may emerge.
footnotes.aripiprazole: One case of torsades de pointes (TdP) and two of QT prolongation reported, and an association with TdP in database studies. Healthy-volunteer data suggest QTc prolongation of about 8 ms. May increase QT dispersion. Low-dose aripiprazole added to another antipsychotic has no effect on QT.
footnotes.olanzapine: Isolated cases of QTc prolongation; acts on the cardiac IKr channel. Other data suggest no effect on QTc.
footnotes.amisulpride: TdP common in overdose; strong association with TdP at clinical doses.

items: Extremes of age: children and elderly may be more susceptible to QT changes

riskFactors.note: Hypokalaemia-related QTc prolongation is more common in acute psychotic admissions. Physical and genetic factors (cardiac potassium channels, CYP enzyme function) may not be found on routine examination but probably predispose to arrhythmia.

groups.extra: Some quinolones affect QTc; see the manufacturer's information.

nonPsychotropics.after: Beta-2 agonists and sympathomimetics may provoke TdP in patients with a prolonged QTc.

rows.action: None, unless T-wave morphology is abnormal
Consider reducing the dose or switching to a drug of lower effect; repeat ECG
Repeat ECG. Stop the suspected causative drug(s) and switch to a drug of lower effect
Review treatment. Consider reducing the dose or switching to a drug of lower effect

references: Taylor DM, Barnes TRE, Young AH. The Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry. 15th ed. Wiley-Blackwell; 2025.
